subject: Interlock: transient p95 jump impacting BrightCart — product asks & customer note
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sylvia Chen <sylvia@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Interlock: transient p95 jump impacting BrightCart — product asks & customer note

Team — quick heads up: BrightCart (account BRG-1247) reported a 3x-7x p95 latency jump on their gen-api traffic starting ~08:50 PT this morning. They see intermittent tail latency and a few timed-out streaming connections. Their SRE reached out to Ben earlier and asked for a timeline.

Initial triage summary:
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (streaming + non-streaming), mostly long-context requests (>1k tokens).
- Customer impact: increased client-side retries, some users hitting 30s+ response times.
- Observed server metrics: p95 spikes, small increase in GPU utilization for a subset of pods, KV cache miss rate up ~18%.

Immediate asks (product + SRE):
1) Karthik — can you confirm any recent kernel-scheduler or batch policy rollouts in us-west-2 in the 07:30–09:00 PT window? If so, we should consider a rollback candidate.
2) Soojin — product question: can we temporarily enforce an aggressive routing policy for BRG-1247 to shift them to a lower-capacity but stable variant (quantized model) while we stabilize? This needs a quick approval path.
3) Marissa/Ben — prepare a short, empathetic customer note that we can send within 90 minutes outlining immediate mitigations and next steps. Keep it high-level; preserve confidence.

I attached a small CSV with annotated p95 deltas and a runbook snapshot.

If we can align on rollback vs routing within 30m I will draft the customer-facing message.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: p95-deltas-annotated.csv (text/csv), runbook-snapshot.txt (text/plain)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interlock: transient p95 jump impacting BrightCart — product asks & customer note

Thanks Naomi — quick update from infra triage: we did push a kernel-scheduler tweak to the continuous-batching path at 07:40 PT that changed the micro-batching threshold for GPUs in us-west-2. Early signals show it improved throughput for small requests but may increase tail for long-context sessions due to batching imbalance.

Triage actions I recommend now:
- Roll back the kernel-scheduler tweak on the affected pool (rollback candidate ready, ETA ~18 minutes).
- Enable protective per-customer QPS throttling for BRG-1247 to cap spike propagation while rollback is in flight (can be applied in <10m).
- Rehydrate KV cache for their hot prefixes (we have a cache-warm job I can run; ~12m).

If Soojin approves routing to a quantized variant as a fallback, that is also an option but will need a short config change on the routing policy and a note about potential accuracy tradeoffs.

I'll start the rollback dry-run now and post logs to the runbook link.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interlock: transient p95 jump impacting BrightCart — product asks & customer note

Appreciate the quick triage. Agreed with the rollback-first approach — prefer to avoid model swaps that could change outputs for BrightCart during peak hours. Two product notes:
1) Routing to the quantized variant is permissible as a last-resort protective fallback but requires an explicit exec approval for BRG-1247 because of their accuracy SLA. Not ideal during a holiday promo window.
2) If rollback completes and we still see >2x p95 we should prioritize:
   - KV cache warming for top 20 prefixes for BRG-1247 (catalog + cart flows).
   - A short-term increase to their burst capacity (dedicated pool burst for 30m) if available — Marissa, can you check contract limits?

Naomi — please draft the customer note to say: we detected a transient performance regression, we are rolling back a recent scheduler change, we have mitigations in flight (throttling + cache-warm), and we'll follow up with a post-mortem and timeline. Keep accuracy/SLAs language conservative.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
VP Product, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: [BrightCart] Interim update: we are rolling back a recent scheduler change (ETA 20–30m)

Sylvia — quick update and apologies for the disruption.

What happened (brief): around 07:40 PT we deployed a scheduler optimization that improved small-request throughput but had an unintended side effect on long-context p95 for a subset of pods. We detected the regression and are rolling back the change now.

Immediate mitigations in progress:
- Rolling back the scheduler tweak (ETA 20–30 minutes).
- Applying protective per-customer throttling to reduce retry storms (in place).
- Running a cache-warm job for your top prefixes (in progress).

What we expect next: if rollback proceeds normally you should see improvement in p95 within ~30–45 minutes. We will follow up with a short post-mortem and any long-term roadmap changes.

We know you’re running a promotion later this week — we are keeping this top priority and will provide another update when rollback completes or sooner if there’s a material change.

If you have any immediate constraints (e.g., planned traffic ramp), please reply here or ping Ben directly and we’ll adjust.

Best —
Naomi

Attachments: p95-deltas-annotated.csv
From: Sylvia Chen <sylvia@brightcart.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [BrightCart] Interim update: we are rolling back a recent scheduler change (ETA 20–30m)

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the transparency and the rapid response. We are seeing improved behavior on our side (p95 dropping toward baseline) after ~25 minutes. Please keep us posted on the post-mortem and any recommended configuration changes we should make.

Also — FYI, our promo ramp is tomorrow at 10:00 PT; if you identify a durable mitigation we’d like to coordinate a deployment/validation window today.

Sylvia Chen
Head of Platform, BrightCart
ops@brightcart.com
